title: The lower truncation image is flat and finitely presented on principal opens inside U
statement: Let X = Spec(A) be affine [def-pc-scheme] and let U be a quasi-compact open subscheme. Let P^\bullet be a bounded-above complex of finite free A-modules [def-pc-perfect-complex] whose associated complex on U represents an object of Tor amplitude in [a,b] [lem-pc-affine-tor-amplitude-criterion]. For an integer r<a, put K = Im(P^{r-1} \to P^r). Then for every f\in A with D(f)\subseteq U, the localized A_f-module K_f is flat and finitely presented. (Equivalently, the restriction to U of the quasi-coherent sheaf \widetilde K is flat and of finite presentation.)

source.place: Tag 08ED proof, paragraph invoking Cohomology, Lemma cohomology-lemma-last-one-flat

proof.text: Fix f with D(f) contained in U. Apply [lem-sc-affine-open-localized-tensor-exact] to get tensor exactness in all degrees below a of the canonical localized complex Q. Its terms are finite free by Module.free_of_isLocalizedModule and Module.Finite.of_isLocalizedModule.

Tensor with the unit and transport exactness by rightUnitorNatIso to obtain Q.ExactAt (r-1). The ModuleCat range/ker characterization gives range(d^(r-2)) = ker(d^(r-1)). Compose opcyclesIsoSc', moduleCatOpcyclesIso, quotEquivOfEq and quotKerEquivRange to identify Q.opcycles (r-1) with the differential image in degree r.

Apply [lem-pc-module-flat-opcycles-tor-criterion] at r-1, using flat terms and tensor exactness at (r-1)-1 < a, and transfer flatness through the preceding linear equivalence. For finite presentation, use the surjection from Q^(r-1) to the image; its kernel is the range of Q^(r-2), a finitely generated submodule. Module.finitePresentation_of_free_of_surjective applies.

The localization functor preserves images. Compose ModuleCat.imageIsoRange, PreservesImage.iso, the functorial imageIsoRange and Shrink.linearEquiv to identify the localized differential image with LocalizedModule.Away f of the original differential image. Transfer Flat and FinitePresentation through that canonical linear equivalence.
